final_answer:
Let

\[
J_p=\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p}\chi(x(x+1)(x+2)).
\]

First shift \(y=x+1\). Since \(\chi(-1)=1\),

\[
J_p=\sum_{y\in\mathbb F_p}\chi(y^3-y).
\]

This is the trace sum of the elliptic curve

\[
E:\quad Y^2=X^3-X,
\]

because

\[
\#E(\mathbb F_p)=p+1+\sum_X \chi(X^3-X)=p+1+J_p.
\]

Now \(E\) has complex multiplication by \(\mathbb Z[i]\), via \((X,Y)\mapsto(-X,iY)\). Equivalently, using a quartic character \(\rho\) modulo \(p\), the Frobenius eigenvalue is the quartic Jacobi sum

\[
j(\rho,\rho)=\sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p}\rho(t)\rho(1-t).
\]

The standard Jacobi-sum evaluation gives

\[
j(\rho,\rho)=u+iv
\]

up to conjugation, where \(p=u^2+v^2\), \(v\) is even, and \(u+iv\) is primary in \(\mathbb Z[i]\), i.e. \(u+v\equiv1\pmod4\). This is exactly the stated sign convention \(u\equiv\varepsilon\pmod4\), since \(v\equiv0\pmod4\) when \(p\equiv1\pmod8\), and \(v\equiv2\pmod4\) when \(p\equiv5\pmod8\). Hence the Frobenius trace is

\[
(u+iv)+(u-iv)=2u.
\]

Therefore

\[
\#E(\mathbb F_p)=p+1-2u,
\]

so

\[
J_p=-2u.
\]

Now compute the two counts. For \(s=\pm1\), let \(N_s\) count triples with all three Legendre symbols equal to \(s\). Expanding,

\[
\sum_x(1+s\chi(x))(1+s\chi(x+1))(1+s\chi(x+2))
=p-3+sJ_p,
\]

because the three linear sums vanish and each pair sum is \(-1\).

For \(s=-1\), the exceptional points \(x=0,-1,-2\) contribute \(0\), so

\[
N_-(p)=\frac{p-3-J_p}{8}
=\frac{p-3+2u}{8}.
\]

For \(s=1\), those exceptional points contribute

\[
(1+1)(1+\varepsilon)+(1+1)^2+(1+\varepsilon)(1+1)
=8+4\varepsilon.
\]

Thus

\[
N_+(p)=\frac{p-3+J_p-(8+4\varepsilon)}8
=\frac{p-11-4\varepsilon-2u}{8}.
\]

Also,

\[
N_+(p)+N_-(p)=\frac{p-7-2\varepsilon}{4},
\]

and

\[
N_-(p)-N_+(p)=\frac{u+\varepsilon+2}{2}.
\]

Therefore the exact pair is

\[
\boxed{
\left(
\frac{p-11-4\varepsilon-2u}{8},
\frac{p-3+2u}{8}
\right)
}.
\]
